messages:
alex: seeing a spike of Pending pods in gpu-heavy jobs, lots of '0/24 nodes are available: Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu' but cluster has idle fractional slices. CA didn't scale. anyone else?
marta: can you paste the pod describe / scheduler events? quick suspicion: fractional requests vs MIG profiles mismatch.
alex: here are the key events: 
```
Events:
  Type     Reason              Age   From               Message
  ----     ------              ----  ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling    2m    default-scheduler  0/24 nodes are available: 24 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu;  -> preemption not chosen
```
config: request: `nvidia.com/gpu: 0.5`, limit: `nvidia.com/gpu: 1` on the same pod (from a helm chart).
chen: ah that pattern. CA won't scale if pod requests don't match node allocatable shapes when we use MIG slicing. Some nodes advertise `nvidia.com/mig-1g.5gb` labels, others are full gpus. Scheduler sees insufficient because the device-plugin reports discrete MIG devices and fractional `0.5` isn't atomic.
kai: also saw CA logs earlier: `Skipping expansion: no unschedulable pods are found` because pods are Pending but not marked unschedulable due to nodeAffinity that filters nodes out.
alex: right — our ML jobs set soft-affinity to prefer `zone: east-1a` which left no compatible MIG nodes in that AZ. Combined with fractional requests, scheduler didn't mark them as scale-triggering.
marta: steps we should try: 1) change requests to match atomic MIG profile (0.25/0.5/1 depending on profile) and remove weird limit>request combos, 2) adjust CA expander to `least-waste` or enable `gpu-binpack` policy, 3) add a fallback nodepool with full gpus in the AZ for burst.
sre-oncall: rolling a quick patch to the helm chart to set `resources.requests.nvidia.com/gpu=0.5` -> `0.5` only works if device plugin maps to 2-slice MIG, otherwise use `1` or specific mig resource name. Recommend using explicit `requests: {"nvidia.com/mig-2g.20gb": 1}` when we have MIG naming.
chen: FYI we also saw wrong admission webhook that normalized requests -> limits; it was bumping requests up to 1 in some cases which caused misfit on half-slice nodes. I filed a PR to stop that.
alex: in the short-term I'm going to cordon the AZ nodes with mismatched MIG profiles and drain jobs to a fallback pool. will also add an alert for 'pending pods due to discrete-gpu mismatch' so we can catch earlier.
kube-bot: deploybot: patch applied to `ml-jobs` helm release in staging (deploy id: deploy-2026-03-18-17). :white_check_mark:
marta: long-term: we should update the autoscaler webhook to treat these pending pods as scale-worthy even if they have nodeAffinity, or add a scheduler-extender that understands our MIG packing rules. also consider packing multiple small jobs into single GPU via job-side proxy to reduce fragmentation.
alex: agreed. i'll open a short RFC with cost/latency tradeoffs for fallback full-gpu pool vs tighter scheduling.
kai: two quick tactical notes: 1) CA scale-up delay is currently 60s in the AZ — bumping to 30s helps on spikes, 2) scale-down granularity should avoid killing GPU nodes with active MIG slices.
chen: adding to RFC: metric to measure 'wasted GPU fractional capacity' and a daily job to simulate binpacking.
sre-oncall: done cordoning on east-1a mismatched nodes, rescheduled ~18 pods into fallback pool. Pending count dropped from 42 -> 6. watch for evictions.
alex: thanks — keep an eye on cost impact for fallback pool. I'll post updates in #incidents if anything regresses. :thumbsup:
